runners_data.name: Esdaile
runners_data.spotlight: 15,000gns foal; by Oasis Dream; fifth foal; half-sister to 1m2f-1m4f winner Jawhary (RPR 82); dam unraced sister to 1m 2yo Group 3 winner Helleborine (dam of good sprinter Calyx) and 6f Group 1 winner African Rose; she has a useful standard to aim at and likely best watched.

runners_data.name: Kino Plasmat
runners_data.spotlight: 250,000gns foal; eighth foal; Wootton Basset half-sister to winners Waikuku (7f-1m1f including multiple HK Group 1s; RPR 124), Waipiro (1m2f including Group 3; 113), It's Good To Laugh (7.3f 2yo/1m4f Flat, 99; 2m-2m3f hurdle) and Dancing Rebel (5f 2yo; 84); dam placed 7f (72); lots to like on paper and he is one to note for market confidence.

runners_data.name: La Mariposa
runners_data.comment: By Zoustar; dam 7f/1m winner (93); unlikely newcomer but market check advised
runners_data.spotlight: 40-1 when a tailed-off last of five on her Newmarket debut eight weeks ago (7f, good); longer-term prospect.

runners_data.name: Starlight Lass
runners_data.spotlight: By Dubawi; first foal of a 1m 2yo winner (RPR 90), herself a half-sister to St Leger winner Logician; stable won the corresponding event last year but with a filly who had experience; betting instructive.

runners_data.name: Sugar Sugar
runners_data.spotlight: Tenth foal; half-sister to five winners including The Night Porter (7f-1m2f including Hong Kong; RPR 95), Wonderful World (6f 2yo; 87) and Dancin Boy (1m-1m2f including Switzerland; 84); dam 7f winner (72), half-sister Irish 1,000 Guineas winner Samitar; apprentice-ridden and sports headgear on debut.

runners_data.name: Yimmna
runners_data.spotlight: 650,000euros yearling by Siyouni; second foal; half-sister to French 9.5f AW/1m2f turf winner Audubon Park (including Listed; RPR 112); dam placed 1m-9.5f in France, half-sister to French 1m4f Group 1 winner Left Hand; lots to like on paper and William Haggas won this race in 2022 (with a newcomer) and 2023; high on the list.

runners_data.name: Quadrillion
runners_data.spotlight: Top-class pedigree and she made a promising start to her career when third of six in a fillies' novice at Newmarket last July (7f, good to firm); odds-on favourite for a Leicester novice one month later when soundly beaten into second but the winner on that occasion is now BHA-rated 112 and finished fifth in the Irish 2000 Guineas; capable of better and she is a strong contender back from a break.

runners_data.name: Shushu
runners_data.comment: From respected Newmarket yard & bred to have bright future; she's one to consider on debut
runners_data.spotlight: Solid start to her career when second of five behind a good prospect at Haydock three weeks ago (7f, soft); open to improvement but may not come into her own until tackling 1m+.

runners_data.name: Victorian Rose
runners_data.comment: Victor Ludorum filly; the betting should prove an accurate indicator for this newcomer
runners_data.spotlight: 80-1 and well beaten on Kempton debut three weeks ago (7f); hard to recommend.

runners_data.name: Sterling Fortune
runners_data.spotlight: Never the slightest threat on her Kempton debut five weeks ago (7f, AW) but only one of the other 13 runners covered the final furlong faster; should do better at some point.

runners_data.name: Too Too Divine
runners_data.comment: Last of four in one AW race; could be a big improver this season, which she needs to be
runners_data.spotlight: Modest form in her two 7f runs, the second of them over C&D six weeks ago (good to firm); might find life easier once handicapping.

runners_data.comment: Improvement needed on third start but southern trainer is 5-9 at Catterick; interesting
runners_data.spotlight: Related to several winners (mostly useful/smart) for her connections; has shown promise at maiden/novice level and looks likely to improve now handicapping with Catterick reappearance under her belt; interesting.

runners_data.name: Komodo Rose

runners_data.name: Jungle Knight
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who needs pace collapse to be effective but showed promise when stepped back from 1m
runners_data.comment: 0-6 at up to 7f and yet to finish better than fourth but has hinted 1m will be a good fit
runners_data.spotlight: Seven-race maiden; shaped a bit better than the bare result, while seeming outstayed over 1m, at Haydock (good to soft) most recently; could go well off a reduced mark back down in trip.

runners_data.name: Blindfold Games
runners_data.note: Prominent runner whose turf form transfer remains questionable after disappointing last start
runners_data.comment: Fair AW form over the winter but this looks tougher back on the grass
runners_data.spotlight: Eight-race maiden who has made the frame a few times over sprint trips on AW; failed to transfer that peak form back to turf (6f) last time; enough to prove back up in distance.

runners_data.name: Miss Starlet
runners_data.note: Tactical prominent performer but form has declined since moving into handicaps
runners_data.comment: Yard been quiet so far this year and she finished well held on her AW comeback
runners_data.spotlight: Six-race career can be split into two contrasting halves, namely steady progress in maidens and steady regress in handicaps; hence a turnaround is required.

runners_data.name: White Ladder
runners_data.note: Lone pace-setter whose third at Salisbury suggests current wellbeing, crucial to race dynamics
runners_data.comment: Improved for nurseries/cheekpieces last summer; up in trip/no headgear on stable debut
runners_data.spotlight: Seven-race maiden; belied his 40-1 odds with 1l third upped to 7f at Salisbury (good) on stable/seasonal debut; possibilities off same mark back down in grade, provided he builds on that effort.

runners_data.name: Blossom In The Air
runners_data.note: Prominent but has fading tendencies and very light weight suggests connections lack confidence
runners_data.comment: Makes her stable/handicap debut after 167 days off; cheekpieces on; much more needed
runners_data.spotlight: Showed no improvement at Lingfield (6f) on stable/handicap/seasonal debut and remains far from solid in form terms.

runners_data.name: Superstorm
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer whose frame finishes suggest readiness for breakthrough effort
runners_data.comment: Placed in both starts since being gelded but well beaten in his two starts on turf
runners_data.spotlight: Nine-race maiden whose consistent 7f form includes making the frame in all three outings this term, latest at Lingfield (good) returned to turf from AW; solid contender who is in the mix.

runners_data.name: Molly Mac
runners_data.note: Prominent 2yo form but 177 days absence creates serious fitness doubts for seasonal return
runners_data.comment: Not threat to front pair when third here on stable debut (7f); tries a new trip today
runners_data.spotlight: Placed in four of her last five 2yo starts but seems rather exposed and is the only runner in this field who lacks recent match practice; makes stable/seasonal debut.

runners_data.name: Inclusive
runners_data.note: Hold-up style needs pace help and first-time cheekpieces represent significant equipment change
runners_data.comment: Third at Southwell on New Year's Day, but twice well held since; look elsewhere
runners_data.spotlight: Inconsistent maiden who has been beaten about 8l in each of her two starts for this yard; first-time cheekpieces need to make a difference.

runners_data.name: Wild Rosie
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer related to stable winners but recent form over various distances lacks conviction
runners_data.comment: Stable/handicap/seasonal debut offered little encouragement last month; cheekpieces go on
runners_data.spotlight: Five-race maiden; faded into sixth of 13 in first-time cheekpieces at Newmarket (1m) most recently; bred to do better still, being related to two winners for her connections; possibilities dropped back in trip.

runners_data.name: Shining Guest
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with weak form who may benefit from handicap debut and 6f specialist tactics
runners_data.spotlight: Thrice-raced filly who has very weak form claims, having beaten a total of only one rival; on the positive side, she may fare better now handicapping with 6f reappearance under her belt.

runners_data.name: Bear Steps
runners_data.note: Prominent style but poor RPRs and first-time headgear represents last-resort stable move
runners_data.comment: Well held in three starts in novice/maiden company; makes her turf/handicap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Showed no improvement switched to handicap level last time, finishing midfield, and still has RPRs in the 30s; chance depends on the effects of first-time headgear.

runners_data.name: Accommodation
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer whose Windsor disaster suggests current confidence issues
runners_data.spotlight: Modest third in final AW attempt and ran dismally (last of 14) upped to 1m at Windsor on handicap/turf debut since; best watched unless the market suggests a bigger effort is likely.

runners_data.name: Jooliah
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner whose 6f background poorly suits this 7f tactical test
runners_data.comment: No impact in four starts last year; big improvement required back from seven months off
runners_data.spotlight: Five-race maiden who has a poor chance on bare figures achieved mostly over 6f; gives 7f another go.

races.paceDynamic: White Ladder emerges as the lone confirmed pace-setter with several prominent racers including Pennine Way, Komodo Rose, Blindfold Games, and Miss Starlet likely to track closely behind. This creates a sustainable tempo rather than destructive early fractions, allowing the pace to be maintained through the middle stages. The combination of soft ground and 7f distance means those who can secure good early positions without over-exerting will hold significant advantages. This race shape clearly favours prominent runners and those with tactical pace who can avoid getting trapped wide or far back in a large 15-runner field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sustainable Pace Holds
scenarios.trigger: If White Ladder sets reasonable fractions without severe pressure from the prominent pack
scenarios.body: The pace becomes truly-run but not destructive, allowing those in the first six to maintain their positions through to the finish. Horses with tactical speed who can secure good berths early will benefit most from this even gallop.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pack Pressure
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent runners (Pennine Way, Komodo Rose, Miss Starlet) pressure White Ladder early
scenarios.body: The early pace quickens beyond sustainable levels, causing the front rank to weaken in the final 2f and creating opportunities for those racing handily. Mid-division horses with finishing kicks benefit from the collapse ahead.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Challenge
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes genuinely slow with White Ladder allowed easy fractions
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish where horses with turn of foot can unleash late challenges from off the pace. Patient tactics and strong finishes become premium assets in a bunched finale.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the 15-runner field creates significant interference and blocked runs in the straight
scenarios.body: Racing room becomes the decisive factor rather than pure ability, favouring those drawn favourably or ridden with exceptional tactical awareness. Luck in running determines the outcome more than form.

watchPoints.text: White Ladder's opening fractions will determine whether prominent runners can settle or must pressure early
Market support for first-time equipment changes on Bear Steps and Inclusive could signal stable confidence
Superstorm's ability to secure cover behind the pace will be crucial given his consistent frame finishes
Any steady early pace will significantly disadvantage the hold-up performers like Jungle Knight and Wild Rosie
The draw and early positioning of Pennine Way and Komodo Rose will reveal their tactical intentions

runners_data.name: Silky Robin
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with excellent recent turf form including soft ground success, ideally positioned for this race shape but is a non-runner
runners_data.comment: Won four races on turf last year and resumes after an unsuccessful stint on the AW.
runners_data.spotlight: Has won on soft and gained his fifth success when winning at Lingfield (5f, good) 22 days ago, making it four wins from his last four starts on turf; steps back up to 6f and he's a contender off this 5lb higher mark.

runners_data.name: Mart
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who can track the pace and has course experience, though carrying a 5lb higher mark than last winning effort
runners_data.comment: There have been some good efforts in his losing run of 16, though not of late
runners_data.spotlight: Seven wins from 47 starts, the most recent success coming at Lingfield (6f, good) last May off an 11lb higher mark; respectable effort when fourth of 12 at Redcar (6f, good to firm) 15 days ago and now needs to build on that.

runners_data.name: Elvetham
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer unproven on ground slower than good, wearing successful blinkers but needs the soft conditions to suit
runners_data.comment: Scored in added blinkers at Lingfield (6f AW) in April; similar efforts (on RPRs) since.
runners_data.spotlight: Unproven on ground slower than good; justified market support when winning in first-time blinkers at Lingfield (6f, AW) in April and has finished third in each of his three starts since, most recently at Thirsk (6f, good) five days ago; solid chance if handling conditions.

runners_data.name: Alafdhal
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning to turf after 120-day break, best over 5f but the strong pace should help his speed
runners_data.comment: Below his best in four starts since his Wolverhampton win in December; off for 113 days
runners_data.spotlight: Last five wins have been over 5f, the most recent at Wolverhampton (AW) in December; below his best in four starts since and now returns to turf for the first time since October 2024 following a 120-day break; best form on grass has been on soft/heavy.

runners_data.name: Albert Cee
runners_data.note: Only confirmed front runner who can control the race, proven over 6f with both turf wins coming on good to soft
runners_data.comment: Back off the same mark as when winning over C&D in January; high on the list
runners_data.spotlight: Didn't get home over 7f at Southwell in March and appreciated the drop to 6f when winning there 20 days ago following a short break; both wins on turf have been on good to soft, and has claims off this 3lb higher mark.

runners_data.name: Court Drive
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer whose sole turf win came on quicker ground, last seen finishing weakly at Southwell 36 days ago
runners_data.spotlight: Sole win on turf came on good to firm at Pontefract last August off 4lb higher; had to switch for a run and couldn't finish strongly enough when last of six at Wolverhampton 36 days ago but shaped as if in form; however, others make a bit more appeal.

runners_data.name: Court Of Session
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with breakthrough turf win at Nottingham seven days ago, has soft ground form and momentum
runners_data.comment: Won readily over 6f on Wednesday and this move back up in trip will suit; respected
runners_data.spotlight: Five-time AW winner who belatedly opened his account on turf when coming from off the pace to win at Nottingham (6f, good) a week ago; has form on ground slower than good and has to be respected under a 4lb penalty.

runners_data.name: Skellig Isle
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer unraced on soft but with stable debut win at Chelmsford showing her ability from off the pace
runners_data.comment: Won on stable debut in March and close fourth of six last time; not ruled out
runners_data.spotlight: Unraced on soft; came from well back to win at Chelmsford (5f, AW) on her stable debut in March and bounced back from a lesser effort when fourth of six at Wolverhampton (6f, AW) last month; however, she was a bit below her best on turf 16 days ago; stable won this last year.

runners_data.name: Big Bard
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with two soft ground wins among his turf victories, returning after 63-day break following poor recent form
runners_data.spotlight: Two of his five wins on turf have been on soft; came back to form when winning at Kempton (6f, AW) in January but he's been well beaten in both starts since; a 63-day break needs to have done him good.

runners_data.name: Kyoto
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer making turf debut after encouraging handicap debut at Southwell, must prove effectiveness on grass
runners_data.comment: Showed ability in three starts at Lingfield; open to improvement on handicap/Tapeta debut
runners_data.spotlight: 0-4 but did shape with some encouragement at Southwell (6f, AW) on his handicap debut 20 days ago after being held up from his wide stall; makes his turf debut and he's open to progress.

races.paceDynamic: Albert Cee is the sole confirmed front runner in this field, meaning he can dictate terms without early pressure over this sharp 6f trip. Mart and Alafdhal may track him in prominent positions, but the majority are hold-up performers including Silky Robin, Elvetham, Court Drive, Court Of Session, Skellig Isle, Big Bard and Kyoto. This creates a moderate pace scenario where Albert Cee can control the fractions before the hold-up brigade launch their challenges in the final two furlongs. The race shape strongly favours horses that can quicken from off the pace, as they'll get the perfect setup to unleash their finishing kicks.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Heroes Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the pace stays steady and Albert Cee isn't pressured early
scenarios.body: The patient hold-up performers get the perfect tactical setup with plenty of horse left for their finishing kicks. Silky Robin's recent turf form and Court Of Session's momentum from his breakthrough Nottingham win make them prime beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Albert Cee gets soft fractions and kicks clear entering the final furlong
scenarios.body: His recent 6f Southwell win shows he has the tactical speed to steal races when unopposed early. The hold-up horses may leave their runs too late on this sharp track.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If Mart or Alafdhal track Albert Cee and pounce late
scenarios.body: They get first run on the leader while avoiding the traffic that often hinders the hold-up performers. Mart's course experience and Alafdhal's 5f speed could prove decisive.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Going Catches Out
scenarios.trigger: If the soft conditions prove more testing than expected for the main contenders
scenarios.body: Horses with proven soft ground form like Big Bard gain a significant edge over those unproven on testing surfaces. The pace could become more genuine if runners struggle.

watchPoints.text: Albert Cee's early position is crucial - if other horses challenge him for the lead the race dynamic completely changes
Elvetham and Skellig Isle are both unproven on soft ground which could be decisive in testing conditions
Court Of Session carries momentum from his breakthrough turf win just seven days ago but faces a quick turnaround
Several hold-up performers including Court Drive and Big Bard return from extended breaks which may blunt their finishing kicks
The 5lb claimer Liam Wright on Albert Cee reduces his effective weight advantage as the likely pace-setter

runners_data.name: Cloudy Rose

runners_data.name: Argentum

runners_data.name: High Favour

races.paceDynamic: Daaris is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field of hold-up horses, creating an unusual tactical dynamic where the leader will face minimal early pressure. With no prominent racers to apply sustained pressure, Daaris can dictate a comfortable tempo through the early stages of this 1m6f test. The lack of pace angles means the race will likely develop into a waiting game, with the large pack of hold-up horses needing to rely on finishing kicks from off the pace. This race shape strongly favours patient hold-up horses with proven finishing speed, as they'll get the perfect setup behind an uncontested leader.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Daaris sets steady fractions without serious challenge through 1m2f
scenarios.body: The pace-setter gets first run on tired legs while hold-up horses face a wall of traffic in the home straight. Daaris exploits the tactical advantage of a solo lead against closers who need everything to fall right.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Kick Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the hold-up brigade times their runs perfectly in the final 3f
scenarios.body: Strong finishers with tactical speed get clear passage and overwhelm a front-runner who has done too much alone. The best finishing kicks decide the outcome in a bunched finale.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If Daaris goes too slow and multiple hold-up horses get racing room simultaneously
scenarios.body: The tempo becomes pedestrian allowing every closer to wind up together, creating chaos but favouring horses with the most natural acceleration. Pure speed from the back trumps position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Fades Early
scenarios.trigger: If Daaris shows early pace but weakens approaching the home turn
scenarios.body: Hold-up horses inherit a tactical race with no genuine pace-setter remaining, suiting patient types who can quicken late. The race becomes a sprint from 2f out.

watchPoints.text: High Favour returning after 75 days with poor recent form - may struggle to handle the pace injection
Daaris hanging right under pressure in recent starts - could compromise finishing effort if challenged
Star Of Jupiter in first-time blinkers and tongue-tie seeking breakthrough performance
Multiple hold-up horses getting racing room simultaneously could create traffic problems in home straight
Captain Robert's consistent recent form makes him key player in any late-developing scenario

runners_data.name: Padua
runners_data.note: Can race freely and make the running but hasn't been seen for 307 days since disappointing effort
runners_data.spotlight: Can race freely, just as he did when making all at Haydock (7f, good) last summer; didn't get away with it at Sandown (7f, good) 307 days ago and he's since been gelded; tongue-tie is removed and he needs to settling better now stepping back up in trip on his reappearance.

runners_data.name: Renewal
runners_data.note: Promising on handicap debut but failed completely when favourite last time out 10 days ago
runners_data.comment: Unexposed 4yo who could have a big part to play back down to 1m on her reappearance
runners_data.spotlight: Record of 4232 in novice/maiden events and ran well when second of 12 on her handicap debut at Newcastle (1m2f, AW) in October; however, she failed to beat a rival home at Thirsk (1m) on her reappearance and needs to take a big step forward from that effort.

runners_data.name: Bella Perla
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare who drops in grade after failing to beat any rivals in two starts this year
runners_data.comment: Better for step up to 1m on AW in 2025, winning two of three; might need this for new yard
runners_data.spotlight: Won a maiden at Southwell (7f, AW) and two 1m handicaps at Lingfield (AW) last year when trained by the Crisfords; drops in grade having failed to beat a rival home on her stable debut at Ascot (1m, good) 32 days ago and has a bit to prove on turf.

runners_data.name: Where's Freddy
runners_data.note: Course-placed hold-up horse but all turf wins came on the July course at Newmarket over 7f-1m
runners_data.comment: Inconsistent last term but some good course form; possible player on his reappearance
runners_data.spotlight: All three wins on turf have been on the Newmarket July course (7f/1m) but he has been placed in two of his three starts over this C&D, including on soft; never featured on his reappearance 25 days ago and needs to build on that.

runners_data.name: Carron
runners_data.note: AW specialist who made it 3-4 on artificial but well below that level in recent turf efforts
runners_data.spotlight: Made it 3-4 on the AW when winning at Newcastle (1m, AW) in March but below that level in two starts on turf since, including when last of his group of five at Newmarket (1m; first-time cheekpieces) 39 days ago; cheekpieces discarded.

races.paceDynamic: Sprightly Dance is the sole confirmed front-runner and will dictate terms uncontested, likely creating a sustainable tempo that suits his style perfectly. With most rivals preferring to hold up (Cavolo Nero, Mythical Guest, Gorgeous Mr George, Bella Perla, Where's Freddy, Carron) and only Percival and Advancing likely to race prominently, the pace will be controlled rather than fierce. The soft ground will emphasize stamina over speed, allowing patient riders to time their challenges from off the pace. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can quicken late, as they'll get the perfect setup from Sprightly Dance's uncontested lead.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Sprightly Dance sets a steady tempo and the field bunches turning for home
scenarios.body: The patient tactics of the hold-up brigade will be rewarded as they get first run on a tiring leader. Gorgeous Mr George's course form and Cavolo Nero's class will tell in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Sprightly Dance finds an unassailable rhythm and kicks clear turning in
scenarios.body: Jack Mitchell can dictate ideal fractions and the 196-day break may have freshened him perfectly. The hold-up horses will have too much ground to make up on the testing surface.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Percival or Advancing can sit close enough to Sprightly Dance without overracing
scenarios.body: The prominent runners avoid the traffic problems that could befall the held-up horses while staying within striking distance. Percival's heavy ground form gives him a key edge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Late
scenarios.trigger: If the soft going takes its toll and multiple horses come with late runs
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint from the two-furlong pole as several hold-up horses challenge simultaneously. Superior finishing kicks will separate the field in a blanket finish.

watchPoints.text: Sprightly Dance could steal this if allowed to dictate his own fractions unchallenged from the front
Gorgeous Mr George drops significantly in class but carries his highest weight since winning here
Percival represents Andre Fabre's stable but hasn't been seen for nearly three months
Multiple hold-up horses could get in each other's way if the pace is too slow early
The soft going may not suit several runners whose best form came on faster surfaces

races.name: attheraces.com/ascot Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: Shaws Phoenix
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits but poor recent AW form for new connections makes her hard to trust despite turf return
runners_data.comment: 0-16 and well held on stable debut/return at Southwell in April; others appeal more
runners_data.spotlight: Maiden who may benefit from the return to turf but otherwise has poor claims on her AW efforts this season for new stable.

runners_data.name: Al Baahy
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with solid classified record on AW but 25 days off and minimal turf experience this season
runners_data.comment: 7yo who has been well held in his last three runs and sole turf win was in May 2023
runners_data.spotlight: Record is only 3-51 but he has form figures of 311 in classified events (all on AW); effective on turf; interesting back at this level.

runners_data.name: Nicely Curved
runners_data.note: Prominent runner but 105 days since last run creates significant fitness doubts despite previous course form
runners_data.spotlight: Maiden whose Flat form for current yard comprises contrasting efforts in two Lingfield AW classified events; not sure what to expect.

runners_data.name: Heer's Sadie
runners_data.note: Three-time course winner whose hold-up style needs stronger pace than likely, but venue experience counts
runners_data.comment: All six wins at either Brighton or Yarmouth; handles most conditions but may need this
runners_data.spotlight: Three-time course winner, including last June/July; could go well returned to this venue with Lingfield reappearance under her belt.

runners_data.name: Girls Allowed
runners_data.note: Prominent 3yo improving with each run and 7lb weight allowance makes her competitively weighted
runners_data.comment: Soundly beaten thus far; makes handicap debut off lowly mark but improvement is necessary
runners_data.spotlight: Showed improvement with fourth-place finish at Leicester (7f) on handicap/seasonal debut; possibilities if building on that effort.

runners_data.name: Contemplation
runners_data.note: Hold-up maiden whose recent longer trips suggest 1m return will suit but overall form remains weak
runners_data.comment: Hasn't threatened in three runs for new yard, taking record to 0-7
runners_data.spotlight: Seven-race maiden whose last two efforts (1m2f) suggest this return to 1m will suit; otherwise has weak claims on overall form.

runners_data.name: Very Demure
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner who can dictate terms unopposed and showed best form at this C&D in cheekpieces
runners_data.comment: First turf start when second over 1m at Yarmouth in cheekpieces latest; claims
runners_data.spotlight: Seven-race maiden who is interesting on her penultimate effort, namely good second in C&D handicap when wearing first-time cheekpieces and just in front of Lady Of Clover on worse terms; now blinkered.

runners_data.name: Lady Of Clover
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with strong recent win and course form, perfectly positioned to strike from off the pace
runners_data.comment: Placed in two of her three starts in 0-55 handicaps including over C&D; much respected
runners_data.spotlight: In-form 3yo who ran well over C&D on penultimate start, then opened her account in Wolverhampton classified contest (8.5f, AW) last week; may improve further at this level; respected even with 6lb penalty.

runners_data.name: Desert Charm
runners_data.note: Previous course winner whose hold-up style needs pace pressure that may not materialize today
runners_data.comment: Sole win came in a classified event last June; isn't sure to be suited by drop back to 7f
runners_data.spotlight: Record is just 1-9 but she gained the win in a division of this race last year (good); ran encouragingly over an inadequate 7f at Southwell (AW) on reappearance; major contender returned to this scenario.

runners_data.name: Harry Don't Bite
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner switching from AW to turf after 77 days off creates multiple question marks
runners_data.spotlight: Not particularly solid on his AW form (five starts); chance largely depends on the effects of this switch to turf.

runners_data.name: Lowestoft
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse showing AW improvement for new trainer but turf form remains unproven
runners_data.comment: No closer than sixth in five starts; tongue-tie on for stable debut; hard to fancy
runners_data.spotlight: Improved AW effort when fourth in Southwell handicap (7f) on stable debut last time; needs to prove he can transfer the form to turf.

runners_data.name: Caitlin G
runners_data.note: Hold-up style with tendency to fade makes her vulnerable over this longer trip despite first-time hood
runners_data.comment: Has failed to beat a rival in all four starts; look elsewhere
runners_data.spotlight: Poor claims on her form over shorter; combination of new trip and first-time hood needs to make a difference.

runners_data.name: Rockafeller Skank
runners_data.note: Hold-up 2yo returning after 222 days and gelding operation makes him hard to assess
runners_data.spotlight: Finished last in three runs last autumn; gelded since; the market signals may help to ascertain whether improvement is likely.

races.paceDynamic: Very Demure appears the only confirmed front-runner in this field, with most rivals preferring prominent or hold-up tactics. This should create a sustainable pace with Very Demure able to dictate terms without significant early pressure from Shaws Phoenix, Girls Allowed, or Nicely Curved who may track behind. The lack of genuine pace pressure means the race will likely develop into a tactical affair with the final two furlongs becoming crucial. This race shape strongly favours horses with tactical speed who can position prominently and kick, rather than pure hold-up horses who may struggle to make up ground in a slowly-run race.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tactical Front-Runner Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Very Demure gets an uncontested lead and dictates a steady pace
scenarios.body: She can use her prominent style to control the race from the front, with her penultimate second at this C&D suggesting she has the tactical speed to respond when challenged. The lack of early pace pressure allows her to conserve energy for a sustained finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent horses can track Very Demure closely and produce superior finishing kicks
scenarios.body: Lady Of Clover or Girls Allowed can use their recent form advantage to strike in the final furlong after stalking the pace. Their younger legs and recent wins give them the tactical edge over the front-runner.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes genuinely strong with multiple horses contesting the lead
scenarios.body: Al Baahy or Desert Charm can use their hold-up style to pick up the pieces, with Desert Charm's previous course win and Al Baahy's classified form giving them the experience. A strong pace would set up perfectly for their closing kicks.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If Very Demure goes too slowly and the field comes to her with a furlong to run
scenarios.body: The race becomes a pure sprint finish where any horse with a turn of foot can win, making it a lottery. This scenario particularly suits horses with recent form who can quicken despite poor positioning.

watchPoints.text: Very Demure must be watched for early pace - if she's allowed to coast in front unchallenged, she becomes very dangerous
Lady Of Clover's ability to get a clean run from her hold-up style will determine if her recent win translates here
Desert Charm needs monitoring for market support given her previous course win and trainer's modest recent record
Girls Allowed should be tracked for position turning in as her prominent style and light weight could prove decisive
Al Baahy's price movement will indicate connections' confidence in his ability to transfer AW classified form to turf
